Very fun indie game with nice graphics, proper stage design and solid gameplay. Though it's still early access, but it got its own style. I am a person who like chopping trees and only the Forest could satisfy me before this game. If you are also a tree chopping person, this game will serve you well. Of course, I think the game still needs some adjustments and more contents like: 1) Cash back function on upgrades (for hardcore players), 2) More intense stages (more enemies / bosses on the screen is always better), 3) More characters (adding Caster, Assassin, Berseker, etc, Ops...just like Fate), 4) Add traps / explosives in the map (random stuffs make the screen more chaotic :) ) 5) Add usage for the woods after the 2nd boss (woods have no use after defeating the 2nd boss. Maybe add a shop / mini-boss before the last boss / just transfer remaining woods to coins?) There are some potentials in this game and I wanna see more in future. Good work guys!!

But the balance is horrid, upgrades feel like nothing despite they can be a bit grindy to get....its a horrible feeling leveling up and seeing available upgrades all DECREASE your damage for small benefits...whats the point in that? 这游戏相比其他的类幸存者游戏，这个游戏采用获取不重复的道具来加强角色，不过当前版本道具量特别少，而且强度差距也非常大，有些道具拿到基本等于通关。比如镜像攻击，比如近战打出气刃。通用打法是前期尽量砍树收集木头，然后打掉第一个首领尽可能升级木头装备，之后升级拿增加攻击范围生命上限和恢复能力的道具，基本就能通关了。 说回来，这游戏目前完成度较低，也就是可以玩的程度，真想成为好的游戏还有相当大的路要走。比如加大角色差异，比如大量设计道具，按照这个游戏一个关卡的升级量，如果能设计出约120种道具，形成20种通关套路，可以够玩30小时，再就是当前版本木头的使用是单一的，可以考虑增加其他的转化途径，增加游戏复杂度。比如说，随机刷新一些特殊怪，时间内消灭后可以获得一次用木头强化已获取道具的机会。同时，武器装备也可以增加升级设定，比如升级到特定的等级时，不获取随机道具，而是可以按技能树选择升级武器装备。 最后，希望游戏能频繁一些更新。至于推荐与否，考虑到10元钱价格，还成吧，总比10元小黄油玩的久。 ----------------- 一年之后，这游戏更新了好多呀，超值！

《In Woods》给我感觉就是一款相较不错的肉鸽游戏，硬要说的话是中规中矩，给七到八分，属于是未来可期的类型。 [h2]先介绍一下游戏吧[/h2] 游戏本身是很有意思、挺好玩的，目前游戏中的道具分为四个种类，分别是魔法道具，神器，制品和独特，而一共有130个魔法道具，20个神器，15个制品和29个独特。 在战斗里可以打树木获取木头，木头可以进行刷新，制作制品等操作；击败敌人，获取经验升级，升级后获得道具；以及游戏结束后获取的金币，用于属性升级。 而我们对角色的属性升级在场外进行，属性有挺多的，例如物理攻击，攻击速度，攻击范围等攻击类型的属性；生命上限，生命回复，防御的防御类型；以及移动速度，经验值增加的其他类型。 [h2]游戏的不足[/h2] 这款游戏的话我个人觉得爽度不够 角色解锁比较繁琐 道具不多，难以凑流派 不知道是什么问题，无法做到无边框全屏 [quote]关注&加入[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32969453/]大众点评[/url]，了解并体验更多好玩游戏[/quote]

It's pretty good, but there are some major balance and pacing issues (as of 1.4) that keep me a little on the fence. There's a good bit of variety and longevity to the progression, and some interesting systems available, but some feel mistuned or undercooked. There are big difficulty spikes between maps and during a run, and sometimes it feels very cheap (a rusher type enemy hits you into a small group following you and you take close to a dozen hits in a second or so and die from nearly fully health). Every character has a melee and a ranged ability, but with most both aren't really viable build paths, and generally melee is the worse one. You gather wood for upgrades but in the course of the 20 minute rounds it's incredibly easy to just harvest all of it and not be able to upgrade at the last couple of upgrade screens (maybe it could use some sort of regrowth or interest mechanic?) The base game sound is incredibly loud (I'm at like 3% and 8% volume sliders.) The item descriptions are not always clear or well explained (what's final critical vs. critical?) The "survivor rank" score screen has to fully animate before you can skip it, and it doesn't actually seem to matter for progression. The damage numbers are big enough to cover up enemies entirely when hitting a lot, but the damage over time numbers are a third the height and are hard to notice (and maybe fire damage is really strong?) There is some good stuff here, and if you like survivorlikes/bullet heavens this will probably scratch the itch, but I find myself frequently frustrated with things that are unclear, feel cheap, or just feel poorly paced. You seem very incentivized to redo early levels for 'prestige' run benefits because the coin payout in later levels can't possibly justify the difficulty spike, but that difficulty spike is also a raw stats check rather than particularly interesting or varied mechanical elements. It seems there are regular updates, so I hope some attention is paid to evening out some of the bumps, glitches, and unexplained mechanics in coming patches.

[h1]Not a bad Survivors-like, but nothing special[/h1] It's not a BAD game at all. In fact, it's kinda decent. The problem is it's lacking a lot of what makes other games in this genre more fun, and that's mostly QOL stuff. There are no indications for where chests (boss upgrades) are when they drop and you walk away from them The boss enemies are just slightly larger sized variants of regular enemies, so it's kinda hard to even notice them sometimes The stages aren't 'infinite' and are within a set arena. This can lead to some chokepoints if you aren't careful Honestly, this has enough to keep people interested if they're die-hard fans. But for the price, it's lacking too much to really make it a MUST BUY. Certain can see value when it's on sale, however. I'd say it's a good game, but not a great one.

I was sent this for free, but don't let that fool you. I wouldn't recommend this to ANYONE, least of all people who are fans of survivorlikes. This is easily the most poorly balanced game in this genre I've played to date. Levels 1 and 2? Easy breezy. I then proceeded to play through level 3 for FIVE HOURS before I finally got a random assortment of cards that actually coalesced together. I spent the entirety of that 5 hours getting demolished by enemies that roll into the arena faster than you can run and then proceed to fire projectiles. You are forced into replaying this single level endlessly just to earn enough coins to level up your metaupgrades from the main menu to survive (and you have to do it on this level because this is the one that gives you a lot more coins than the first 2; cool right?). Oh also everything in this level takes minimum 7 hits to kill. All enemies, not just elites. Then you get to level 4, the final level, and the problems compound. If you don't get lucky and get enough cards that deal damage, you will inevitably be overrun by bats that fire 3 projectiles each, creating a clusterf*** that not even the most seasoned bullethell aficionado can wiggle out of. You are limited to a very specific set of cards in order to actually succeed. Vampire Survivors at least gives you the ability to survive and succeed with multiple different builds. This game? Meta or get tf out. There's also no 1440p support which, in 2024 when this released, is absolutely baffling. I would strongly recommend that nobody play this pile of garbage.

[h1]In Woods: Survival in a Haunted Forest[/h1] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bsvHXopoOZk In Woods throws you into a dark forest crawling with monsters, where survival depends on gathering resources, crafting tools, and fighting through endless waves of enemies. Each run lets you level up, pick upgrades, and experiment with different builds to push a little further. The pixel art gives the world a gloomy atmosphere, and the constant pressure of enemies keeps the pace quick and tense. Crafting adds a nice layer on top of the combat, making progress feel rewarding. Still, as with many roguelikes, repetition sets in — some runs can feel too similar once you’ve seen most of the upgrades. Finished the Game 100% in 18,5 hours.

I've only played for about 70 minutes, but that's enough time to get a feel for this type of game. Honestly, I'm on the fence as to whether I would recommend this game; however, because I purchased it for $4 and it's an independent game, I'm OK. giving it a bit of leeway. Pros: * Lots of characters that you can unlock. Some (not all) are different enough to add a sense of variety. * Persistent upgrades * Vampire Survivor-esque gameplay, with appropriate skills and combos to be had * Price - The regular price is in the $7 range, which is not unreasonable Cons * Graphics aren't good, especially the interface; it's amateurish * There's a lack of QoL features - no UI directing you to points of interest and the health bar isn't near your character are some examples * The levels are big squares with black borders * Bosses are just larger versions of minions If they flesh this game out a bit (similar to the Pathfinder version of this genre, which I recommend), I'd give this a much stronger review.
